answer:
Growing rice on this field has a low suitability score of 13 out of 100 [S1]. The field has severe limitations for rice production, primarily due to soil pH and drainage conditions [S1]. 

The soil pH is 8.8 (SSURGO soil survey), which is well above the optimal range of 5.5 to 7 for rice [S2][S1]. Additionally, the field is classified as well drained (SSURGO soil survey), whereas rice is optimal in poorly drained soils that remain saturated for more than half the year [S2][S1]. 

Water availability is another major challenge. Rice requires an optimal annual rainfall or water supply of 1500 to 2000 mm [S2][S1], but the mean annual rainfall at this location is 288 mm (ERA5 reanalysis (ECMWF), daily aggregates, 25 km pixel, modelled, 2006-2025). While irrigation can supply the water deficit, the high pH and well-drained sandy loam soil (SSURGO soil survey) make this field poorly suited for flooded rice cultivation [S3].

Have a soil test performed to confirm the exact local pH and nutrient status before considering major soil amendments.
